newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks close lower as bonds dive.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks close lower as bonds dive.

text.p: The Australian share market ended lower on Monday, sold down as weakness in a bruised and battered bond market flowed through to equities.
At 4.30 p.m. (0630 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 10.8 points at 2,282.1.
The September share index futures were 24 points down at 2,286, a 3.9 point premium to the index.
Brokers said with the Dow holding up relatively well, given the mauling bonds received on Friday, local players had sounded a note of caution ahead of a possible delayed Dow reaction later today.
"People are hesitant ahead of Wall Street tonight," said Jamie Spiteri, dealer at Shaw Stockbroking.
"While bonds in the U.S. came off, the Dow held and people are cautious ahead of what could be more action there tonight."
Features were hard to find with the continuing profit season stealing most of the attention.
First off the rank was aluminium producer Comalco which saw its shares tumble after a sharply lower first half net profit of A$50.6 million on a joint venture basis.
Shares in Fosters Brewing ended flat after it reported a 2.2 percent higher full year net profit of A$293.3 million.

Spicers Paper shares closed off a cent after reporting a 35 percent fall in full year net profit to A$16.02 million while plumbing and building materials supplier G.E. Crane reported a 15 percent drop in full year net profit to A$20.54 million.
Hills Industries closed weaker after a 1.5 percent higher full year net profit of A$12.22 million and forecasts of difficult growth in 1996/97.
Boardroom ructions saw timber producer Auspine's shares lose ground while gold explorer Bendigo Mining rose on the back of a report of new gold resources at its tenemnets in Victoria.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to six, while about 37 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, bonds fell sharply in late trading as the market corrected the steep rally of the past few weeks, he initial sell-down triggered by a slide in U.S. Treasuries on Friday. The 10-year bond ended at 8.10 percet, up 0.23 point.

The Australian dollar subsided to a steady finish in what was rapidly becoming a well worn pattern of fruitless rallies and frustrated profit taking. Traders said the repeated failure to break US$0.7935 resistance left the currency vulnerable to a selloff back to US$7850. At 4.45 p.m. it stood at $0.7910/15.
